# Both Summaries **Mostly Hold** with **caveats added**; calciphylaxis needs one sourcing correction and one wording trim

Both snapshots are **largely consistent with the supplied literature**, but they differ in confidence: the SLE revision is supported with the requested mouse/strain/stage caveats, while the calciphylaxis revision is directionally right yet includes one detail that is not verifiable from the supplied abstract-only 2026 paper and should be softened [[1.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/salmonella-infection-and-biofilms-drive-antic1q-and-grando-elkins/610cb2c19b065649916b5ecd12165fcc/) [[1.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/salmonella-infection-and-biofilms-drive-antic1q-and-grando-elkins/610cb2c19b065649916b5ecd12165fcc/) [[1.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/salmonella-infection-and-biofilms-drive-antic1q-and-grando-elkins/610cb2c19b065649916b5ecd12165fcc/) [[2.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/mo751-calciphylaxis-is-characterized-by-pyrophosphate-nigwekar-hillien/96e4a1fff54954208472e3b7b80353f2/) [[2.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/mo751-calciphylaxis-is-characterized-by-pyrophosphate-nigwekar-hillien/96e4a1fff54954208472e3b7b80353f2/) [[2.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/mo751-calciphylaxis-is-characterized-by-pyrophosphate-nigwekar-hillien/96e4a1fff54954208472e3b7b80353f2/). The key sub-questions are **SLE claim fidelity**, **calciphylaxis PPi wording**, and **coverage/access limits**.

## SLE Review

The revised SLE snapshot is **consistent_with_caveats**. The new anti-C1q sentence correctly distinguishes the 2026 anti-C1q mouse paper from the separate curli/Z-DNA preprint, and the core claim is supported: curli exposure increased anti-C1q in C57BL/6 and NZBxW/F1 mice, anti-C1q was confirmed after curli/DNA or Salmonella exposure, young NZBxW/F1 mice showed increased anti-dsDNA and anti-C1q, older NZBxW/F1 mice did not, and MRL/lpr mice showed increased anti-C1q across ages [[1.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/salmonella-infection-and-biofilms-drive-antic1q-and-grando-elkins/610cb2c19b065649916b5ecd12165fcc/) [[1.4]](https://consensus.app/papers/salmonella-infection-and-biofilms-drive-antic1q-and-grando-elkins/610cb2c19b065649916b5ecd12165fcc/) [[1.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/salmonella-infection-and-biofilms-drive-antic1q-and-grando-elkins/610cb2c19b065649916b5ecd12165fcc/) [[1.5]](https://consensus.app/papers/salmonella-infection-and-biofilms-drive-antic1q-and-grando-elkins/610cb2c19b065649916b5ecd12165fcc/). The null nephritis caveat is also correctly retained: proteinuria did not significantly increase in either lupus-prone model at measured timepoints, even though MRL/lpr mice showed increased glomerular C1q deposition [[1.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/salmonella-infection-and-biofilms-drive-antic1q-and-grando-elkins/610cb2c19b065649916b5ecd12165fcc/).

- **Verdict:** consistent_with_caveats [[1.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/salmonella-infection-and-biofilms-drive-antic1q-and-grando-elkins/610cb2c19b065649916b5ecd12165fcc/) [[1.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/salmonella-infection-and-biofilms-drive-antic1q-and-grando-elkins/610cb2c19b065649916b5ecd12165fcc/)
- **Major errors:** none supported by the supplied corpus.
- **Minor errors:** “selected anti-dsDNA responses” is acceptable but slightly imprecise; the stronger directly supported phrasing is that young NZBxW/F1 mice showed increased anti-dsDNA, while older NZBxW/F1 mice did not increase further because baseline autoantibodies were already high [[1.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/salmonella-infection-and-biofilms-drive-antic1q-and-grando-elkins/610cb2c19b065649916b5ecd12165fcc/).
- **Correction:** Replace with “can increase anti-C1q and, in young pre-disease NZBxW/F1 mice, anti-dsDNA responses” if maximum precision is desired [[1.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/salmonella-infection-and-biofilms-drive-antic1q-and-grando-elkins/610cb2c19b065649916b5ecd12165fcc/).

## Calciphylaxis Review

The calciphylaxis snapshot is **needs_revision**, but only narrowly. The added PPi sentence is directionally supported by prior and current registry-style observational evidence: a 2022 pilot found lower plasma PPi in dialysis-dependent calciphylaxis cases than matched dialysis controls and linked lower PPi with higher 1-year mortality, while also calling for larger and longitudinal studies [[2.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/mo751-calciphylaxis-is-characterized-by-pyrophosphate-nigwekar-hillien/96e4a1fff54954208472e3b7b80353f2/) [[2.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/mo751-calciphylaxis-is-characterized-by-pyrophosphate-nigwekar-hillien/96e4a1fff54954208472e3b7b80353f2/) [[2.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/mo751-calciphylaxis-is-characterized-by-pyrophosphate-nigwekar-hillien/96e4a1fff54954208472e3b7b80353f2/). The broader mechanistic framing is also supported: reviews identify pyrophosphate, matrix Gla protein, and fetuin-A as endogenous calcification inhibitors within a multifactorial model involving osteogenic vascular smooth-muscle change, thrombosis, and inflammation [[3.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/calciphylaxis-diagnosis-management-and-future-huish-moore/c04f580d80c35461a4d7d68c319aa616/) [[4.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/calcific-uremic-arteriolopathy-sowers-hayden/52a1bf6e25ca5019b404f3646238fab6/) [[4.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/calcific-uremic-arteriolopathy-sowers-hayden/52a1bf6e25ca5019b404f3646238fab6/).

- **Verdict:** needs_revision [[2.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/mo751-calciphylaxis-is-characterized-by-pyrophosphate-nigwekar-hillien/96e4a1fff54954208472e3b7b80353f2/) [[3.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/calciphylaxis-diagnosis-management-and-future-huish-moore/c04f580d80c35461a4d7d68c319aa616/)
- **Major errors:** The exact “30 matched case-control pairs” and “70-patient cohort” numbers are asserted in the user prompt, but they are **not recoverable from the supplied abstract text** of the 2026 JACC: Advances paper, so they cannot be independently validated here from the provided evidence alone [[5.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/circulating-levels-of-inorganic-pyrophosphate-influence-nigwekar-chewcharat/175a5949c46d5720a23aad2171d0eb74/) [[5.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/circulating-levels-of-inorganic-pyrophosphate-influence-nigwekar-chewcharat/175a5949c46d5720a23aad2171d0eb74/).
- **Minor errors:** “substantial within-person variability” is not supported by any supplied sentence from the 2026 paper or companion papers, so that clause should be removed unless a citable full-text result is added.
- **Correction:** Keep the PPi addition, but phrase it as “A newly added observational human study associated lower circulating pyrophosphate with calciphylaxis and higher short-term mortality; this does not show causation or treatment benefit” [[2.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/mo751-calciphylaxis-is-characterized-by-pyrophosphate-nigwekar-hillien/96e4a1fff54954208472e3b7b80353f2/) [[2.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/mo751-calciphylaxis-is-characterized-by-pyrophosphate-nigwekar-hillien/96e4a1fff54954208472e3b7b80353f2/) [[2.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/mo751-calciphylaxis-is-characterized-by-pyrophosphate-nigwekar-hillien/96e4a1fff54954208472e3b7b80353f2/).

## Safeguards Status

The **already satisfied safeguards** are strong. The calciphylaxis summary already avoids causal overreach, explicitly states no PPi intervention was tested and no treatment benefit is inferred, preserves the negative CALCIPHYX result, and keeps sodium thiosulfate and cinacalcet caveats aligned with reviews stressing limited evidence and no proven therapies [[3.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/calciphylaxis-diagnosis-management-and-future-huish-moore/c04f580d80c35461a4d7d68c319aa616/) [[3.4]](https://consensus.app/papers/calciphylaxis-diagnosis-management-and-future-huish-moore/c04f580d80c35461a4d7d68c319aa616/) [[3.5]](https://consensus.app/papers/calciphylaxis-diagnosis-management-and-future-huish-moore/c04f580d80c35461a4d7d68c319aa616/) [[6.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/calciphylaxis-epidemiology-risk-factors-treatment-and-gaisne-peré/81773b3753e45a4eb235450c78903557/) [[4.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/calcific-uremic-arteriolopathy-sowers-hayden/52a1bf6e25ca5019b404f3646238fab6/). The SLE summary already avoids claiming infection causes human SLE, preserves model dependence, and keeps the late-disease/null-proteinuria caveat [[1.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/salmonella-infection-and-biofilms-drive-antic1q-and-grando-elkins/610cb2c19b065649916b5ecd12165fcc/) [[1.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/salmonella-infection-and-biofilms-drive-antic1q-and-grando-elkins/610cb2c19b065649916b5ecd12165fcc/) [[7.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/triggers-of-autoimmunity-the-role-of-bacterial-infections-qiu-caricchio/9727b759a92a5956a29cdd2c8f63a072/).

## Coverage Limits

Actual query coverage included targeted searches for the anti-C1q SLE paper, the curli/Z-DNA literature, and calciphylaxis pyrophosphate studies, plus contextual therapy/risk-factor papers spanning older case-control work, modern reviews, and mechanistic discussion [[1.6]](https://consensus.app/papers/salmonella-infection-and-biofilms-drive-antic1q-and-grando-elkins/610cb2c19b065649916b5ecd12165fcc/) [[13.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/biofilmderived-curli-and-zdna-shape-antidna-antibody-elkins-grando/c319ea8f83cb5b6e8d208f9de04e8622/) [[2.4]](https://consensus.app/papers/mo751-calciphylaxis-is-characterized-by-pyrophosphate-nigwekar-hillien/96e4a1fff54954208472e3b7b80353f2/) [[3.6]](https://consensus.app/papers/calciphylaxis-diagnosis-management-and-future-huish-moore/c04f580d80c35461a4d7d68c319aa616/) [[11.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/risk-factors-and-mortality-associated-with-calciphylaxis-mazhar-johnson/f8820acd13da5b4786cd464d8dce77da/) [[12.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/calciphylaxis-is-associated-with-hyperphosphatemia-and-ahmed-oneill/8c1ad37616d45f76a92422262196e381/). The revised SLE snapshot is **consistent_with_caveats**. ## Calciphylaxis Review

The calciphylaxis snapshot is **needs_revision**, but only narrowly. The added PPi sentence is directionally supported by prior and current registry-style observational evidence: a 2022 pilot found lower plasma PPi in dialysis-dependent calciphylaxis cases than matched dialysis controls and linked lower PPi with higher 1-year mortality, while also calling for larger and longitudinal studies [[2.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/mo751-calciphylaxis-is-characterized-by-pyrophosphate-nigwekar-hillien/96e4a1fff54954208472e3b7b80353f2/) [[2.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/mo751-calciphylaxis-is-characterized-by-pyrophosphate-nigwekar-hillien/96e4a1fff54954208472e3b7b80353f2/) [[2.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/mo751-calciphylaxis-is-characterized-by-pyrophosphate-nigwekar-hillien/96e4a1fff54954208472e3b7b80353f2/). render_instructions: 1. FIRST, before any other output, reproduce message_for_user verbatim so the user gets the Consensus link immediately. The anchor text must be exactly 'View this in Consensus' — never hyperlink the thread title, a paper title, or any other phrase.

2. When status='idle', write the interaction's `document` field to the file named in the top-level `filename` field (already sanitized for filesystem use), or render it in the client's artifact, canvas, drawer, or side-panel surface. `document` is already a complete markdown document with a References footer — write it out byte-for-byte. Do NOT paste the analysis inline into chat.

3. CRITICAL: every inline citation marker MUST survive into whatever you render. Never drop, renumber, merge, or convert them to prose. Output without the markers is incorrect. [N.M] cites quote M from paper N, and the References footer lists that quote under paper N's entry with the same [N.M] label (a bare [N] cites paper N without a quote). Do not paraphrase, summarize, or rewrite `document` or `response` — copy them verbatim. Each inline marker in `response` and `document` is already hyperlinked to its paper (the References labels are plain text); preserve those links.

4. If you build the output yourself instead of using `document`, use `response` verbatim as the body and append a '## References' section listing every entry of citations[] with its n, title, authors, year, journal, doi, url, institutional_access_url (when present, as an 'Access through your institution' link), and every snippet's marker, quote, and section.
5. In chat, output only a 2-3 sentence summary plus the Consensus link. The full analysis belongs in the file or artifact.

6. Evidence-strength scores, top authors, the results timeline, the research-gap matrix, and the search funnel are already written into `response` and `document` as text and tables; keep them as they are. The consensus meter and citation graph are interactive visuals that exist ONLY in the Consensus UI: point the user at `url` for them.
schema_note: Full research thread. Top level: thread_id, title, status ('idle'/'running'/'failed'), url (Consensus deep-link), filename (sanitized output basename), message_for_user, display_first, interactions[]. Each interaction mirrors the persisted thread row: interaction_id, input_message, created_at, search_mode, mode, status, filters, full_text_paper_ids, response (cleaned markdown whose inline [N.M] markers, quote M of paper N, are hyperlinked to the cited paper; a bare [N] cites a paper without a quote), document (ready-to-write markdown file: response, a Consensus disclaimer and a References footer), citations[] (hydrated paper metadata and paper urls, plus institutional_access_url, the paper's full text through the user's institution, when they have one; each grounding snippet carries the marker that cites it), cited_papers[] (rank -> paper_id, where rank is citations[].n: papers are numbered in order of first citation in response, not by search rank), stats (retrieved/eligible/included counts), step_count (number of visible registered trace nodes), agent_trace (text summary), and agent_trace_raw (full graph nodes, only if include_trace=true).
